invariants: Every new or changed English string gets a Welsh draft beside it in the same change, as the service's other copy does.

Every changed page works fully without JavaScript: every state change is a form post, every search and filter a form with a button that submits it, and JavaScript only enhances a page that already works (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 6; conflicts:c-006).

A behaviour is built with GOV.UK Frontend first, then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); no custom JavaScript is written to copy the prototype, pop-ups are not built and confirmations stay pages (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 5, 7 and 19).
Pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components and govuk-* classes; the prototype's custom app-dr2-* blocks are not copied.

A search box is the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select and behaves as the real frontend configures it; its entries are what MDM serves through reference-data, and only how the list reads follows the prototype (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 1 to 4).

Where a row changes a page or behaviour the high-risk plants frontend also has, the same increment changes plants too: plants mirrors the structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour, and keeps its own questions, data and step order (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 43 and 44).
Shared wording in a frontend's shared copy is never reworded in place; a set-specific string goes in the feature's own copy (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 41).

Notification statuses are only ever added, never renamed or removed, and each new status is mapped in every frontend that reads it before the animals backend first sends it (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 42).
A page in its error state keeps the 'Error: ' prefix on its browser title (conflicts:c-006).

Every save control a page offers makes exactly the same checks on that page's answers, with no page an exception: a missing or invalid answer keeps the trader on the page with an error for each one and what they entered still shown, and the controls differ only in where they go once every answer passes (ruling:sam-2026-10-26).
Notifications, templates and address book entries stay scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates); nothing lists another organisation's records.
Each increment updates the tests repo's specs, page objects and journey helpers its change breaks, in the same change.

A change to a high-risk plants page, obligation or behaviour lands its own update to that set's journey specification, its decisions ledger entry and any guide that describes it, in the same increment as the change.

increments.title: Germinal Commodity details asks the quantity, the number of packages where it applies, the total gross weight and the temperature, the record holds them, and every trade line says what it is
increments.detail: The germinal set's copy of Commodity details asks, for each chosen species, a required quantity in units or pieces; for a species whose commodity is a semen, embryo or ova line on the data fields page's package-count list, an optional number of packages; and an optional total gross weight in kilograms. It always asks one optional temperature for the whole page. Germinal species are counted by quantity, never by head. A germinal commodity has one Selected commodities row listing all its chosen species, and its block is headed by the commodity's name and code. The animals backend holds the quantity, the number of packages and the gross weight on each species line, the weight as a decimal, and the one temperature answer on every commodity line, and shows them back. Each published trade line's quantity is its quantity in units or pieces; the weight and the temperature are not published, because the profile the service publishes against carries no field for either. While the commodity data still holds a combined embryos-and-ova line, each germinal trade line carries an interim type code taken from the line's product type, so a combined line records its ova as embryos.
acceptanceCriteria: Each germinal species block on Commodity details asks 'Total gross weight', after 'Quantity (unit/pieces)' and any 'Number of packages', in a narrow text input with the suffix 'kg', on every germinal species block whatever its commodity; left blank it shows no error and saves. increments.title: The germinal start and its main import reason: two reasons, four purposes, the Transit answers and no exit date
increments.detail: A germinal products notification is started from the germinal set's own start, which creates the draft without asking the notification type question and opens at the set's origin page; from there the trader runs through 'What are you importing?' and the main import reason to Commodity details as live animals does. The germinal set asks no exit date: the live-animals set keeps its own. A reason or purpose outside the lists the page offers is never saved.

increments.title: Germinal identification dates and names: text inputs with a 'Choose date' calendar, and the format, real-date and length checks
increments.detail: On the germinal identification page the collection and production dates are each a single text input with an example hint, so the page works fully without JavaScript, and a 'Choose date' calendar sits over each input to enhance it. The donor name or identification and the identification number or mark are each capped at 58 characters, and each date must be given as a day, month and four-digit year and must be a real date. Nothing else is checked: any real date, past or future, is accepted, a one- or two-digit day and month are accepted, and the production date is never compared with the collection date. When several answers fail, the errors are listed in the order the fields are asked, each linked to its own field.

increments.title: Germinal Commodity details checks the quantity and the weight, and lists its errors by question
increments.detail: The germinal set's Commodity details page checks the figures it asks for. The quantity is required and must be a whole number from 1 to 1,000. A total gross weight, when given, must be a number greater than 0, at most 1,000 kilograms and to no more than two decimal places, with spaces around the figure ignored. Where the design gives the message it is used, and the rest follow the GOV.UK pattern for a maximum. Each error is linked from the error summary to that species' field and shown inline, with what was entered kept. The error summary lists its errors by question: every quantity error, then every number of packages error, then every total gross weight error. A blank number of packages, a blank total gross weight or an unanswered temperature saves.
